title: Microsoft 365 admin center: agent-level controls for pay-as-you-go

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing treats the newer Cost Management spending policies as implemented controls for Copilot Chat and SharePoint agents, although Microsoft documents those services separately. In particular, leaving an agent outside a resource-based policy does not guarantee that it cannot incur charges. The default state and executable API call also need correction.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; controls[0] applicability; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: The cited newer Cost Management identity/resource spending policies implement much of the roadmap's agent-level controls for Copilot Chat and SharePoint agents.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat, SharePoint Agents, or Microsoft Copilot Retrieval API (Preview), see Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service overview.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that these documents establish shipment of this roadmap item. Separate the newer dashboard's supported-service and Copilot Studio controls from classic Chat/SharePoint billing. For the latter, cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/setup-pay-as-you-go and https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/sharepoint-agents-azure-billing; describe agent-level availability as the roadmap plan, not an established equivalence.

claims.claim: Identity-based spending policies govern supported users and groups and can have per-user limits.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies can limit Copilot Studio agents or environments.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Widespread pay-as-you-go SharePoint agent use can generate spending without an enforced budget cap.
claims.quote: the system doesn't enforce the budget or prevent your organization from exceeding it. Usage can continue uninterrupted even after the budget is surpassed

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Site owners can create SharePoint agents when the relevant agent access requirements are met.
claims.quote: Members of your organization can build SharePoint agents if they have access to SharePoint and the tenant has been enabled as pay-as-you-go for SharePoint, or they have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
claims.fix: Cite this creation guidance and retain its prerequisite of SharePoint access plus a Copilot licence or enabled SharePoint pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: When SharePoint pay-as-you-go is configured, an eligible unlicensed colleague's use of a SharePoint agent draws on the billing resource.
claims.quote: That resource is used whenever a user without a Microsoft Copilot license uses a SharePoint agent.
claims.fix: Add this feature-specific source and say 'eligible user with access to the agent' so tenant-wide billing is not mistaken for overriding file permissions.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents respect users' existing data permissions.
claims.quote: They can answer questions, summarize content, and perform tasks based on user permissions.

claims.claim: DLP and sensitivity labels can govern the content SharePoint agents use.
claims.quote: To prevent selected files from being used by agents, use sensitivity labels along with Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
claims.fix: Cite this page and make the scope explicit: this is content protection for SharePoint agents, not a feature of the billing control or a sensitivity label placed directly on an .agent file.

claims.claim: The roles that can create the relevant billing policies are Global Administrator and Billing Administrator.
claims.quote:
You must have one of the following roles to complete the tasks in this article:

    - Billing Administrator
    - AI Administrator
    - Global Administrator
claims.fix: Separate classic Chat/SharePoint billing-policy roles from newer spending-policy roles. For classic setup, include AI Administrator and the required Owner or Contributor rights to the Azure subscription and resource group, as stated at this URL.

claims.claim: AI Administrators and License Administrators can edit newer spending-policy limits and alerts.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods. However, they can't create spending policies.
claims.fix: Identify these as newer spending-policy permissions, not classic agent billing-policy permissions. Note that the same source also lists License Administrator among read-only consumption roles and says those roles cannot change limits or alerts; do not present that role's effective rights as unqualified.

claims.claim: Membership of a policy's scoped groups determines access to credit-consuming services.
claims.quote: You can now add more spending policies to scope access to specific groups, users, or services.

claims.claim: Agents themselves may take actions even though the feature discussed is a billing control.
claims.quote: They can answer questions, summarize content, and perform tasks based on user permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enabling tenant-wide service billing can enable metered agent access for the covered population.
claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users. Optionally, you can customize the default spending policy to specific groups or change the services it governs

claims.claim: Users without a licence who are excluded from a policy see agents that they cannot use.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Chat agents excluded billing policy visible'; 'SharePoint agents see pay-as-you-go not access'. Opened pay-as-you-go overview, SharePoint agent access and Copilot Chat agent management; none states this excluded-user visibility behaviour.
claims.fix: Remove the assertion that excluded users see the agents. Retain the analysis as 'Explain eligibility and access requirements to users to reduce support questions.'

claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report gives an example of 10 credits for tenant-graph grounding on a prompt.
claims.quote: 10 credits for tenant graph-grounding
claims.fix: Keep this explicitly as the report's example and identify the report documentation's preview qualifications rather than implying a final universal per-prompt tariff.

claims.claim: The same worked example adds 2 credits for generative answers.
claims.quote: two credits for generative answers
claims.fix: Retain the example framing and state that the report documentation includes preview qualifications; do not present this as a universal charge for every interaction.

claims.claim: The Copilot Credits report alerts on users exceeding 2,000 credits.
claims.quote: the report includes alerts when users in your organization use more than 2,000 credits.
claims.fix: Mention that these report alerts are documented with preview qualifications. Distinguish the similar 2,000-3,000-credit alert from the Alerts card documented for more than 3,000 credits in the past 30 days.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agent spending can be managed through the newer Microsoft 365 Cost Management experience or existing Power Platform controls.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.
claims.fix: Cite this source and explain that coverage by a Microsoft 365 resource policy changes which admin center's spending controls apply.

claims.claim: Leaving agents outside resource-based spending policies makes those agents not billable.
claims.quote: Environments that aren't linked to a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy continue under their applicable Power Platform configuration during the opt-in period.
claims.fix: Delete 'leave the rest uncovered so they are not billable'. For Copilot Studio, explain the fallback to existing Power Platform billing and review all applicable policies. For Chat/SharePoint, use documented service billing connections and agent access permissions; do not promise a resource-policy allowlist for this roadmap item.

claims.claim: The newer spending policies provide administrator alerts and user-level threshold notifications.
claims.quote: If a monthly per-user limit is configured, set the user-level notification thresholds. These notifications alert users as they approach their spending limit

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Administrators can inventory agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant admins and AI admins can manage actively used agents in SharePoint in the Microsoft 365 admin center, under the Agents section of the Copilot Control System
claims.fix: Cite this page and qualify the SharePoint view as actively used agents visible through Copilot Chat; it is not proof of a complete inventory of every unused .agent file.

claims.quote: Billed amounts are updated daily and sometimes more frequently. It can take 24 hours after usage of a service to show in Microsoft Cost Management.

claims.claim: Azure Cost Management does not provide the Copilot credit-policy configuration control.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Azure Cost Management Copilot spending policies control'. Opened View costs and billing, usage-based billing setup and SharePoint agent billing. These locate credit-policy configuration in Microsoft 365 and describe Azure cost analysis, budgets and alerts, not a credit-policy editor.

claims.claim: The Power Platform individual-agent limit applies to agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: A tenant may need controls in both Microsoft 365 and Power Platform admin centers.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.
claims.fix: Cite this page and add the precedence qualification: different scopes may require review in both centers, but Microsoft 365 policies take precedence for covered usage; do not imply two independent additive caps.

claims.claim: Government-cloud rollout dates for this roadmap item's new agent-level control have not been published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'SharePoint agents GCC pay-as-you-go'; '496363 default agent level controls pay as you go'. Read the roadmap record and Microsoft pay-as-you-go overview and government-availability search excerpts; no government launch date for this new control was returned.

claims.where: Open questions: Government cloud availability of pay-as-you-go for agents
claims.claim: Government-cloud availability of the underlying pay-as-you-go service is an unpublished question.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 pay-as-you-go is not available for Office 365 government plans or Office 365 operated by 21Vianet to and for PRC-located users.
claims.fix: Report this published service restriction, citing the terms page, while keeping future government rollout dates for the new roadmap control as not published. Do not equate an unknown future date with unknown current service availability.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Graph Cost Management API is a beta API rooted at /copilot/costManagement and covers spending policies and consumption.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... through Microsoft Graph, rooted at /copilot/costManagement. ... spending policy management ... usage reports that break down consumption by user, security group, governed service, and funding class.

claims.claim: No other programmatic route for the newer Microsoft 365 credit spending policies is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Cost Management spending policies PowerShell API automation alternative Microsoft Graph'. Opened Cost Management API overview and usage-based billing setup; results document Graph, not another equivalent spending-policy interface.

claims.where: front matter: action; front matter: risk; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The prepare action fits a new optional control rated medium risk.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; schema: 'review: an optional capability, or a new control, that changes nothing until an admin or maker chooses it.'
claims.fix: Set action to 'review' for this optional new control. The schema's prepare exception requires an unconfigured control closing an exposure rated high, which is not the page's rating.

claims.fix: Add an agent-inventory/access-management row scoped and qualified using https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/manage-access-agents-in-sharepoint, or remove the inventory instruction if the briefing cannot provide its documented control.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout and After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The controls table includes Azure budget alerts and cost analysis used by the checklist.
